title: Scaling regression surgery and proofpoint remediation for dedicated throughput shortfall
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: During a 2026-02-28 customer workload surge we observed a sustained dedicated-pool throughput shortfall (~25-40% under committed RPS for two hours) caused by an autoscaler regression combined with degraded scheduling heuristics. This ticket coordinates the immediate remediation ('surgery') and the follow-up proofpoint work to validate fixes and prevent regressions. Impact: multiple committed tenants experienced elevated p99 latency and token queueing despite healthy GPU utilization; revenue-impacting SLA exposure. Hypothesis: a recent autoscaler change widened the target CPU headroom thresholds and disabled a fallback for tenant-isolated pools, which interacted poorly with kernel scheduling prioritization for long-sequence traffic. Scope: triage, hotfix candidate, telemetry enrichment, runbook updates, unit/regression tests for autoscaler logic, and a short-term mitigation layer in fleet control (tenant throttles & emergency headroom reserve). Success criteria: restore committed throughput to >=98% of SLA baseline within 24h of remediation; add deterministic unit/regression tests; +3 observability signals to detect similar regressions within 5 minutes.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Chen: Triage call summary. We confirmed correlation between autoscaler change (PR #4387) and the incident window. Diego will own hotfix branch; SRE to prepare emergency headroom knobs.

2026-03-02 - Diego Ramirez: Created hotfix candidate that reverts widened headroom threshold and restores legacy fallback for tenant-isolated pools. Running e2e against the synthetic-stress harness. Draft PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4412.

2026-03-03 - Maya Singh (SRE): Deployed hotfix to one staging shard; observed throughput recovery on staging load profile A (long sequences + KV-heavy). Will run 6h soak and then promote to limited prod canary (10% of committed pools).
2026-03-05 - Diego Ramirez: Canary went green for 12h; telemetry shows p99 latency reduced 42% for impacted tenants. Merging hotfix after code review from Rohan. Follow-ups listed below.
2026-03-07 - Product (Eliot Hargrave): Noted customer escalations; coordinating proactive outreach and credits for affected tenants. Need a clear timeline for permanent mitigations.

2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Began proofpoint work: added synthetic workloads that exercise corner cases (mixed short/long sequences, KV caching warmups) to the regression harness; added alerts for autoscaler divergence and scheduling anomalies.
postmortem_notes: Immediate: rolled back autoscaler threshold change for tenant-isolated pools and restored legacy fallback path; deployed emergency headroom reserve policy (5% per shard) to reduce blast radius. Short-term: add canary gating for autoscaler config changes, extend regression harness with long-sequence KV-cold profiles, and add an autoscaler divergence alert (ratio of expected vs observed capacity > 15% for >5m). Long-term: redesign autoscaler decision path to include workload shape classifier, expose tenant-level latency SLOs into autoscaler feedback, and canonicalize a rollback-safe deployment flow for fleet control. Owners: Diego (hotfix + tests), Maya (soak & SRE validation), Rohan (autoscaler redesign RFC).
